title: Rav Yehoshua
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Pesachim 53b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.53b): “Rav Yehoshua said: Rava expounded.” Perhaps he was the father of the well-known Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua. Dikdukei Soferim records an omission at “Rav Yehoshua.” In [Shabbat 151b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.151b.5) we find: “Rabbi Levi said: Rav Pappi said: R' Yehoshua said: After three days his belly splits open,” etc.[^2] There the reading should be R' Yehoshua of Sikhnin, as explained in his entry.[^1]

notes.text: The proposed father-son identification and the correction to Yehoshua of Sikhnin are Hyman’s, with “perhaps” preserved. The contextual patronymic in רב הונא בריה דר״י is expanded as Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua without assigning an external identity. דק״ס is the customary abbreviation for Dikdukei Soferim. Hyman writes ליתא תיבת רב יהושע; this may concern the complete designation or just Rav before Yehoshua. “An omission at” avoids the earlier English’s unjustified restriction to Rav alone while leaving the exact extent unresolved. The repeated א״ר clauses are kept as successive “said” attributions; no additional transmission links are supplied. The pronoun “his” has no newly supplied antecedent. The printed locators נג: and קנא: conventionally give 53b and 151b. The Pesachim passage has not been independently checked here; the Shabbat passage was checked for the titles, as explained below.

Hyman abbreviates the titles in this chain. The checked William Davidson vocalized Hebrew edition of [Shabbat 151b:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.151b.5) explicitly reads רבי לוי, רב פפי and רבי יהושע. This supports Rabbi Levi and Rav Pappi at this occurrence. The last name is kept as R' Yehoshua in the abbreviated quotation because this notice discusses the reading under the heading Rav Yehoshua and proposes a correction to Yehoshua of Sikhnin. The checked edition’s Rabbi Yehoshua and Hyman’s textual argument are separate evidence; neither is an automatic identification of the speaker. R' preserves the unresolved title where the English otherwise would choose one.
